selection.rationale: Circuit Atlas uses editable native diagrams and data visuals to carry architecture, lifecycle, enterprise evidence, and market-layer relationships without presenting a developer preview as a mature enterprise product. It scores highest for expert audience fit, information density, asset availability, and accessibility.

candidates.name: Circuit Atlas
candidates.rationale: Audience 5/5, Topic 5/5, Brand 4/5, Density 5/5, Assets 5/5, Accessibility 5/5. Deep navy, signal cyan, and modular nodes encode control and event flow.

candidates.name: Open Source Editorial
candidates.rationale: Audience 4/5, Topic 4/5, Brand 5/5, Density 4/5, Assets 5/5, Accessibility 4/5. Warm editorial contrast is readable but weaker for dense architecture and state relationships.

candidates.name: Enterprise Blueprint
candidates.rationale: Audience 4/5, Topic 4/5, Brand 3/5, Density 4/5, Assets 5/5, Accessibility 5/5. Conventional blue-and-white styling risks overstating enterprise maturity.

motif.name: Signal path
motif.description: Use a 2–3 pt signal-cyan line to connect deep-navy rounded nodes. Highlight at most one node per slide to show events, capabilities, or control moving through the system.
rules: Signal lines encode causal, data, or control relationships and are never decorative.
Use signal fill or outline on at most one primary node per slide.
Section slides use one ascending path; content slides show only the local relationship needed for the takeaway.

image_style.description: The deck uses PowerPoint-native diagrams, editable shape compositions, tables, and number callouts. Screenshots are allowed only when the interface itself is evidence.
image_style.crop_rule: Crop screenshots to 16:9 or 4:3 while preserving relevant interface context; never stretch.
image_style.treatment_rule: Use 0.08 in rounded corners, a 1 pt surface border, and no shadow on screenshots; keep diagrams editable.
image_style.credit_rule: Place external source and license at 9 pt in the footer; credit native synthesis to the cited official source.
image_style.ai_generation_rule: Do not use AI images by default. If a concept requires one, use a consistent deep-navy technical cutaway style and never generate text, data, logos, trademarks, or interfaces.

icon_style.description: Use only line icons assembled from PowerPoint basic geometry: 2 pt strokes, no gradients, deep navy or cyan, and consistent rounded containers.

chart_style.description: Label the conclusion directly; use secondary for the main series, accent for the key series, and risk for exceptions. Keep labels at least 12 pt and preserve a zero baseline when relevant.

table_style.description: Use primary/white headers, background/text bodies, alternating surface rows, necessary horizontal rules only, right-aligned numbers, and text labels in addition to color.

layouts.description: Six columns of title and version context on the left; a native-shape plugin orbit around the control plane on the right.
A causal statement on the left and a Model–Harness–environment control diagram on the right.
Four question nodes arranged along one ascending signal path.
A dark section slide with a large chapter number, one conclusion, and one native-shape composition.
A horizontal barrier-controlled loop with the key authority and ordered-commit nodes emphasized.
Five Cordis primitives around Plugin runtime with one lifecycle boundary callout.
A Host-to-interface plugin stack crossed by one shared lifecycle axis.
Host plane, one standing Preset scope, and multiple Session Agent scopes.
Four translucent ordered configuration sheets with explicit override direction.
Append-only events, a versioned checkpoint row, and three replayed projections.
Definition, Provider registry, Consumer, and Agent with policy interception and a separate subprocess path.
Agent/Session core surrounded by CLI, Web, Headless, ACP, and SDK transport boundaries.
Host source, Typert, metadata, registry, and Client in a five-stage build pipeline.
Immutable Package and Run state machine with page wait, approval, activation, render, repair, and rollback.
Progressive Runtime local, Data path, and Control evidence containers.
Agent surrounded by six explicit security and data boundaries with covered/not-covered labels.
Five-row enterprise verification matrix with priority and public evidence status.
Three market layers labeled by buyer, value, representatives, and switching cost.
Three-column China competitor matrix plus a broken attention-to-revenue inference axis.
Frozen inputs split into two systems and reconverge at evidence, scoring, explanation, and repetition.
A strategic conclusion supported by Architecture, Governance, and Evidence plus a 30/60/90-day action staircase.

do: Give every slide one retellable conclusion and prefer conclusion-led titles.
Build the primary visual with editable native shapes, charts, or tables.
Give every arrow a causal, data, or control meaning.
Reserve a 9 pt footer for fixed commit, compact source label, and market retrieval date.
Encode risk and state with text and shape as well as color.
dont: Do not use decorative color bars, title underlines, meaningless gradients, glass effects, or glow.
Do not fill whitespace with generic stock photos of handshakes, lightbulbs, puzzles, or robots.
Do not repeat one composition for three consecutive slides or reduce the deck to a card wall.
Do not present stars, forks, or vendor claims as enterprise adoption, revenue, or compliance evidence.
Do not set body text below 17 pt or solve overload by shrinking type.
